ownedComment.body: Ordner im Modellbaum auswählen --> ALT+B
Fährt das Fahrzeug und interagiert aktiv mit dem Bremssystem.
Wartet und repariert das Bremssystem.
Unterhält das Fahrzeug und ist primär an den jeweiligen Kosten zum betreiben des Fahrzeugs interessiert.
ALT+B --> Ordner im Modellbaum finden

nestedClassifier.name: Fähig an allen Rädern zu wirken
Bleibt aktiviert trotz ABS und ASR

ownedComment.body: Verstärkt die Fahrer aufgebracht Bremskraft.
Stellt die grundlegenden Assistenzsysteme (ABS, ESP, ASR) bereit.
Erkennt verschiedene Störungen des Bremssystems.
Verzögert die Radumfangsgeschwindigkeit der Räder um damit die Fahrzeuggeschwindigkeit zu reduzieren.
Kommuniziert mit dem Fahrzeugsteuergerät um Infomrationen über zum Beispiel Störungen weiter zu geben.
Überwacht den Verschleißzustand der Bremsbeläge.
Verhindert das Blockieren der Räder bei einer Bremsung.
Stabilisiert das Fahrzeug und verringert aktiv durch Bremseingriffe Unter- und Übersteuern.
Verhindert ein übermäßiges Durchschleudern der Antriebsräder durch einen Bremseingriff.
Erkennt eine Gefahrenbremsung und unterstützt den Fahrer eine Vollbremsung einzuleiten.
Überwacht den Bremsdruck der einzelnen Kreise und meldet bei zu großen Differenzen.
Setzt den Bremsdruck in eine Kraft um die die Räder verzögert.
Führt die Wärme aus dem Reibungsbremsvorgang an die Umwelt ab.
Partikel die durch das Reibungsbremsen entstehen, werden aus dem Bremssystem abgeführt.
Überwacht die Funktionsfähigkeit des Anti-Blockier-Systems.
Überwacht die funktionsfähigkeit des elektronischen Stabilitätsprogramms.
Überwacht die funktionsfähigkeit der Feststellbremse.
Meldet Störungen an das Fahrzeugsteuergerät.
Sichert das Fahrzeug bzw. das Gespann gegen wegrollen.
Erfasst die Eingabe die Feststellbremse zu schalten.
Schaltet den Zustand der Feststellbremse um.
Erzeugt aus der Bremskraft einen übertragbaren Bremsdruck.
Überträgt den Bremsdruck.

Properties:Properties_of_Feather_Nut_Con.Disadvanatges: Braking Operations With Forward And Reverse Rotation is not possible.
Limited strength. so not suitable for high torque application.
Stress concentration occur due to keyway slots in shaft and adapter.
Properties:Properties_of_Feather_Nut_Con.Advantages: The key prevents relative rotation between the shaft and the hub, allowing reliable transmission of torque without slippage.
The use of a nut and washer to secure the hub makes the assembly easy to install and remove, especially for maintenance or replacement.
Feather keys are standard machine elements and relatively inexpensive to manufacture and install.

Properties:Properties_of_Feather_Nut_Con.Disadvanatges: Braking Operations With Forward And Reverse Rotation is not possible.Limited strength. so not suitable for high torque application.Stress concentration occur due to keyway slots in shaft and adapter.

Properties:Properties_of_Conical_fit_con.Advantages: The tapered shape naturally centers the components during assembly, improving alignment and reducing runout — especially important in rotating applications.
The fit holds the parts together without the need for bolts, pins, or adhesives, simplifying assembly and maintenance.
The interference fit creates a vibration-resistant and rigid assembly with minimal backlash, ideal for high-speed or high-precision applications.
Properties:Properties_of_Conical_fit_con.Disadvantages: Due to repeated tightening of nut, the surface of shaft is get damaged.
The tapered geometry can leads to localized stress concentration.
Under cyclic loads, conical fits may get loosen
Braking Operations With Forward And Reverse Rotation is not possible.Limited strength. so not suitable for high torque application.Stress concentration occur due to keyway slots in shaft and adapter.

Properties:Properties_of_Ring_clamping_e.Disadvantages: The space constrain due to size and shape of ring clamping element.
Not well suited for significant radial loads.
Properties:Properties_of_Ring_clamping_e.Advantages: Eliminates the need for machining keyways, simplifying shaft and hub design and reducing stress concentrations.
The clamping force is evenly distributed around the shaft circumference, reducing the risk of stress concentrations and fatigue failure.
Can be installed and removed without special tools or heating/cooling processes. Maintenance and replacement are straightforward.

Properties:Properties_for_Screws_connect.Advanatges: Allows axial positioning of the hub anywhere along the shaft during assembly — useful in prototypes or adjustable designs.
No need for keyways or splines, reducing machining costs and time.
Screws are inexpensive and easy to install using standard tools, making them ideal for cost-sensitive or simple assemblies.
Properties:Properties_for_Screws_connect.Disadvantages: Screws can loosen over time due to vibration, thermal cycling, or repeated loading.
Threads or contact areas may wear over time.
To ensure continued reliability, screw connections may require periodic checking or re-tightening, especially in dynamic or load-cycling environments.

Properties:Properties_for_Real_bearing_A.Advantages: Axial force absorption on both sides
Good guidance under eccentric loads Ideal for varying braking forces

Properties:Properties_for_fix_and_loose_.Advantages: Compensates for thermal expansion of the shaft
Properties:Properties_for_fix_and_loose_.Disadvantages: Axial force absorption on one side only

Properties:Properties_for_X_configuratio.Advantages: Axial force absorption on both side
Properties:Properties_for_X_configuratio.Disadvantages: lower tilting stiffness than O configuration

Properties:Properties_for_Drum_brake.Disadvanatages: Not suitable for high-speed or high-performance vehicles

Properties:Properties_for_left_mounting_.How_it_works: Friction Pads inside of brake caliper are push against brake disc during braking.

Properties:Properties_for_Top_mounting_b.Disadvantages: Limited modularity of the braking system
Lever arm longer than the side

Properties:Properties_for_Below_mounting.Advantages: Maintenance easier than above brake caliper
Cooling system design easier to implement
Properties:Properties_for_Below_mounting.Disadvantages: Limited modularity of the braking system
Properties:Properties_for_Below_mounting.How_it_works: Brake Caliper pushes against direction of travel.

sysml:Requirement.Text: “The test bench shall generate controllable rotational motion and apply braking forces to the brake system under test.”
The system shall allow braking operations with both forward and reverse rotation, including the reversal of the rotational direction of the brake component.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Test Bench itself

sysml:Requirement.Text: Drum brakes can generate high braking force with relatively low hydraulic pressure due to the self-energizing effect.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Product Test Case

sysml:Requirement.Text: The braking system test bench shall support braking force or equivalent braking torque levels in a controlled and repeatable manner, enabling evaluation of braking behavior under different braking intensities across all operating modes.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Test Bench itself

sysml:Requirement.Text: “The test bench shall simulate vehicle driving conditions and external influences acting on the brake system.”
Parking brake mechanism can be easily integrated into the drum brake assembly without requiring additional systems

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Product Test Case

sysml:Requirement.Text: The second electric machine shall simulate realistic road load conditions including rolling resistance, aerodynamic drag, and gradient forces

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Product Test Case

sysml:Requirement.Text: The second electric machine shall apply both positive and negative torque to simulate uphill, downhill, and braking conditions.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Product Test Case

sysml:Requirement.Text: The validation environment shall validate blended braking with hydraulic ABS braking and recuperative braking.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Product Test Case
RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.category: Test Bench with ABS & Recuperative Braking

sysml:Requirement.Text: The validation environment shall enable operation over varying wheel slip conditions such as dry, wet, and icy roads

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Product Test Case

sysml:Requirement.Text: The system shall support repeated braking cycles with variable brake force without the rotating brake component coming to a complete stop.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Test Bench itself

sysml:Requirement.Text: The second electric machine shall include protection mechanisms to prevent damage under overload, excessive slip, or unexpected torque spikes during test scenarios.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Product Test Case

sysml:Requirement.Text: The validation environment shall provide signals required by the ABS controller.
The validation environment shall support closed-loop interaction between rest vehicle simulation and brake system with its behaviour.
The system shall allow emergency braking operations decelerating a rotating brake component from 50 km/h to 0 km/h using the maximum available brake force

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Test Bench itself

sysml:Requirement.Text: It shall be possible to change the friction conditions by applying defined fluids (e.g., oil, water) without requiring extensive modifications to the setup.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Product Test Case

sysml:Requirement.Text: Drum brakes can be packaged more easily within smaller wheel sizes compared to disc brakes, supporting compact vehicle designs.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Product Test Case

sysml:Requirement.Text: The system shall simulate emergency braking maneuvers at varying speeds to assess ABS effectiveness in reducing stopping distance

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Product Test Case

sysml:Requirement.Text: The validation environment shall support integration of an external brake ECU.
It shall be possible to change the friction conditions by replacing the friction material without requiring major changes to the test environment.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Product Test Case

sysml:Requirement.Text: “The test bench shall remain structurally safe, mechanically stable, and manufacturable under all operating conditions.”
The test bench shall allow easy installation, adjustment, and exchange of brake systems under test

sysml:Requirement.Text: The brake caliper holder shall minimize the lever arm relative to the braking force to reduce structural loads.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Product Test Case

sysml:Requirement.Text: The brake caliper holder must allow quick repositioning of the brake caliper in all three spatial directions using elongated holes or equivalent adjustment features.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Product Test Case

sysml:Requirement.Text: The validation environment shall allow the ABS controller to actively modulate brake pressure.
The test bench shall allow rapid modulation of brake torque to validate ABS response during lock-up prevention

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Product Test Case

sysml:Requirement.Text: The validation environment shall provide a hydraulic circuit including ABS components.
The mechanical interface shall allow simple exchange of the brake system under test using standard tools, without major structural modifications.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Product Test Case

sysml:Requirement.Text: All physical components of the system shall be manufacturable using conventional techniques such as turning, milling, laser cutting, and welding.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Test Bench itself

sysml:Requirement.Text: The system shall prevent resonance effects from vibrations induced by braking forces or other actuators such as electric machines.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Test Bench itself

sysml:Requirement.Text: “The test bench shall measure, record, and allow control interventions during braking tests.”
All load-bearing components shall be designed to withstand the maximum expected operational loads without failure or critical crack formation.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Test Bench itself

sysml:Requirement.Text: The system shall monitor the temperature of the brake disc during operation to ensure safe operating conditions and prevent thermal overload.
The brake caliper must be mounted laterally to the brake disc to enable compatibility with different brake system geometries.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Product Test Case

sysml:Requirement.Text: The system shall record recovered energy, braking torque distribution, wheel slip, and stopping distance to evaluate ABS and recuperative braking performance

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Product Test Case
RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.category: Test Bench with ABS & Recuperative Braking

sysml:Requirement.Text: The validation environment shall acquire vehicle dynamics signals required for brake system validation (e.g. longitudinal acceleration, yaw rate and steering angle
The bearing arrangement should have maximize tilting rigidity and effectively absorb external forces and torques applied outside the bearing span (from the electric machine and braking system).

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Product Test Case

sysml:Requirement.Text: It tends to increase preload as the shaft expands (due to heat), which can be beneficial in high-temperature environments where stability is required.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Product Test Case

sysml:Requirement.Text: More tolerant of misalignment between shaft and housing.
The bearing concept shall support the radial and axial forces applied without introducing mechanical overconstraints or preload under normal operating conditions.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Product Test Case

sysml:Requirement.Text: The validation environment shall synchronously acquire all relevant measurement signals required for brake system validation.
The spread of the contact lines (large effective span between load centers) gives the system greater resistance to tilting and bending moments.

Framework_Profile_SysML:Stakeholder_Nutz.Text: Das System soll das wegrollen des Fahrzeugs/Gespanns verhindern können
Das System soll dem Fahrer in grundfunktionen assistieren können
System soll auch unter geänderten Umständen den funktionsumfang größtenteils erhalten
Störungen im System sollten selbstständig erkannt und kommuniziert werden
Das System soll durch seine sicherheitsrelevanz auch zuverlässig sein
Verschmutzungen sollten möglichst automatisch abgetragen werden
Das System soll das Fahrzeug dosierbar verzögern können

sysml:Requirement.Text: Sensors (e.g., force, temperature, rotational speed) shall be placed close to the system under test while being protected against brake dust, heat, and fluids.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Test Bench itself

sysml:Requirement.Text: All rotating components shall be designed to withstand the maximum operating speed without structural failure, excessive vibration, or critical resonance.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Test Bench itself

sysml:Requirement.Text: The validation environment shall provide accurate wheel speed measurements required for ABS control and validation.

RequirementTaggingProfile:TaggedRequirem.Classification: Requirement derived from Product Test Case

Framework_Profile_SysML:funktionale_Anfo.Text: Erkennt eine Gefahrenbremsung und unterstützt den Fahrer dabei eine Vollbremsung einzuleiten
Nur eine Eingabeeinrichtung darf vorhanden sein. Muss das Bremsen ermöglichen während beide Hände am Steuer sind.
Muss die Muskelkraft auf ein Maß erhöhen, sodass die geforderten Bremswerte erreicht werden
Gesamtfahrzeug sowohl verzögern als auch feststellen können

Framework_Profile_SysML:nicht_funktional.Text: Muss aus Metall gefertigt sein, falls Versagen eine Hilfsbremsung unmöglich macht
Muss gegenüber Alterung und Korrosion Standfest sein

Framework_Profile_SysML:funktionale_Anfo.Text: Verschleißbedingte Toleranzen müssen automatisch ausgeglichen werden

Framework_Profile_SysML:nicht_funktional.Text: Bremskraftverteilung zwischen Achsen muss in anbetracht der Fahrzeugdynamik sinnvoll gewählt werden

Framework_Profile_SysML:funktionale_Anfo.Text: Aufteilung in Betriebsbrems- und Hilfsbremssystem. Dabei muss HBS noch funktionsfähig sein wenn nicht mehr als eine Störung im BBS vorhanden ist
Fahrzeug stabilität muss immer sichergestellt sein
Hat das blockieren der Räder zu verhindern um Lenkbarkeit und Stabilität sicherzustellen

Framework_Profile_SysML:nicht_funktional.Text: Bremsbeläge müssen frei von Asbest sein

mdElement.text:
Disadvantages:

  • The space constrain due to size and shape of ring clamping element.
  • Not well suited for significant radial loads.
  • Most expensive
Screws are used to increase the press between the connection of the adapter and shaft. Also, there is thread connection

Advantages:

  • Eliminates the need for machining keyways, simplifying shaft and hub design and reducing stress concentrations.
  • The clamping force is evenly distributed around the shaft circumference, reducing the risk of stress concentrations and fatigue failure.
  • Can be installed and removed without special tools or heating/cooling processes. Maintenance and replacement are straightforward

mdElement.text: Physical Principle: Pressing by tightening the screws
Physical Principle: Pressing by tightening the screws
Mounts brake disc to Rotating shaft(Main shaft)
Provides the Interface for attaching the caliper Holder
the base plate gives it a solid foundation so braking force doesn’t shake or move the parts.
Transfer Clamping force from caliper pistons to pads
Pushes the Friction pads towards the brake Disc
Fluid from the master cylinder directly go to brake caliper and Pressure fully depends on driver’s foot
Friction Converts Kinectic energy into heat & slows the wheel
Supports the inner side of rotating shaft & Handles smaller loads
Supports the Outer side of Rotating shaft & Handles larger Loads
Hydraulic Pressure Interface supplying controlled brake pressure to master cylinder inlet

Advantages:

  • Allows axial positioning of the hub anywhere along the shaft during assembly — useful in prototypes or adjustable designs.
  • No need for keyways or splines, reducing machining costs and time.
  • Screws are inexpensive and easy to install using standard tools, making them ideal for cost-sensitive or simple assemblies.

Disadvantages:

  • Screws can loosen over time due to vibration, thermal cycling, or repeated loading.
  • Threads or contact areas may wear over time.
  • To ensure continued reliability, screw connections may require periodic checking or re-tightening, especially in dynamic or load-cycling environments.

mdElement.text: Frictional force fit physical connection with tighteing the screws
Frictional force fit physical connection with tighteing the screws
Frictional force fit physical connection with tighteing the screws
Frictional force fit physical connection with tighteing the screws
Physical Principle: Pressing by tightening the screws
Physical Principle: Pressing by tightening the screws
Non-contact magnetic sensing (Provides Speed signal interface).
Sends wheel speed data as an Electrical signal and control interface
Mounts Brake Disc to Main shaft
Provides the interface for attaching the caliper holder
the base plate gives it a solid foundation so braking force doesn’t shake or move the parts.
Sends brake line Pressure data as an Electrical signal
Transfer clamping force from caliper pistons to pads
Pushes the friction pads towards brake disc
Fiction converts kinectic energy into heat , slowing the wheel
Supportsinner side of rotating shaft & handles smaller loads
Supports outer side of rotating shaft & handles larger loads
Hydraulic Pressure Interface supplying controlled brake pressure to master cylinder inlet
Simulated desired Wheel Speed, Longitudinal Acceleration, desired Brake pressure, Yaw Rate, Steering Angle,
Conical ends of both shaft and adapter are fixed to each other with frictional force fit

Disadvantage:

  • Due to repeated tightening of nut, the surface of shaft is get damaged.
  • The tapered geometry can leads to localized stress concentration
  • Under cyclic loads, conical fits may get loosen

Advantages:

  • The tapered shape naturally centers the components during assembly, improving alignment and reducing runout — especially important in rotating applications.
  • The fit holds the parts together without the need for bolts, pins, or adhesives, simplifying assembly and maintenance.
  • The interference fit creates a vibration-resistant and rigid assembly with minimal backlash, ideal for high-speed or high-precision applications
Tightening Nut is used to increase the pressing of the connection between adapter and shaft. Also, there is thread connection

mdElement.text: Welding is carried out to fixed the screws in small shaft.
There is a clearance between the screws and holes of the screws in rotor of measurement technique. (No direct physical connection)

Disadvantages:

  • Braking Operations With Forward And Reverse Rotation is not possible.
  • Limited strength. so not suitable for high torque  application.
  • Stress concentration occur due to keyway slots in shaft and adapter.
Nut to hold the position of brake adapter, prevents from sliding due to forces and it has thread connection
Spacer sleeves to fill void between the nut and brake adapter and it has Form Fit physical connection

Advantages:

  • The key prevents relative rotation between the shaft and the hub, allowing reliable transmission of torque without slippage.
  • The use of a nut and washer to secure the hub makes the assembly easy to install and remove, especially for maintenance or replacement.
  •  Feather keys are standard machine elements and relatively inexpensive to manufacture and install.
Physical Principle: Pressing by tightening the screws
Physical Principle: Pressing by tightening the screws
Pedal signal ( Force and Pedal Position Sensor )
Vehicle Dynamics ( Wheel speed, Yaw rate, Motor speed)
Torque Request ( Total braking Torque , regenerative /friction split, ABS brake demand )
